Proposing a test: **Sufficient Identity**

My kid should be able to contact her grandparents to get bailed out of jail in another country.

And tech should assist my elderly parents to discern whether it's actually their grandkid or not.

---

Playing with the idea that the most human (humane) form of online identity is Ephemeral Identity.

Allows people (and things!) to recognize you, until you no longer want them to. Shared agency and trust, with control remaining mostly with the individual.

Natural choices we make irl (and their url counterparts):
- Irish goodbye (don't log on any more)
- change hair style / hair color (change your PFP)
- cosmetic surgery (make a new login)

Malignant AI bots, and creepy *systems* used to track people, have a hard time with this. Whereas, teenagers in gamer chatrooms, and adults in big cities who go to bars and dinner parties with strangers, all learn how to move.
